scope_description.value: Electrical coordination study for the pump electrical distribution system at the Raw Water No. 2 Treatment Plant. Scope included: (1) field survey of Pumps #2, #3, and #4 and generation of system model using SKM Power Tools; (2) short-circuit study of the pump electrical system; (3) coordination of tripping characteristics of overcurrent protective devices. Study followed ANSI/NEMA MTS-2019 paragraph on Coordination Studies scope. Key finding: selective coordination is impossible with existing devices; compromised coordination is the achievable objective. Recommendations: set 200A MCB instantaneous trip to High/maximum position; upgrade to 200A MCB with adjustable/static trip for near-coordinated system.
scope_description.source: Study introduction and Recommended System Modifications section
scope_description.quote: Bowman, Foster & Associates, Inc. (BFA) was tasked with performing a coordination study on the electrical distribution system for the Gloucester Water Treatment Plant Pump #2, 3, & 4.

value: Three pole-mounted 50 kVA transformers/transformer bank with 480V secondary
Low-voltage ATS with 200A main circuit breaker (Square D type JGL-36200T), adjustable instantaneous trip
Pump #2 and #3: 50A circuit breakers, GE type TED13050, fixed setting
Pump #4: 100A circuit breaker, GE type TED13100, fixed setting
key_equipment_surveyed.source: Study introduction and Time Current Curves section
key_equipment_surveyed.quote: The existing system is comprised of a utility feed serving the three pole mounted 50 kVA transformers/transformer bank with 480 V secondary. This transformer bank feeds low voltage ATS with the main circuit breaker (MCB). Pumps circuit breakers are connected to the ATS through the wireway.

utility_assumption.value: 3-phase 100 MVA utility contribution; single line ground (SLG) 30 MVA
utility_assumption.quote: the Utility Contribution was assumed as 3-phase 100 MVA and Single Line Ground (SLG) as 30 MVA

key_finding.value: Selective coordination is impossible with the existing 200A MCB and pump branch circuit breakers. Compromised coordination per ANSI/NEMA MTS-2019 is the achievable objective. No equipment failed the Equipment Evaluation (all fault currents within ratings).
key_finding.source: Time Current Curves section and Equipment Evaluation Report
key_finding.quote: Pumps circuit breakers cannot be selectively coordinated with 200 A main circuit breaker (MCB) at all.

recommendation.value: 1) Set 200A MCB instantaneous trip to High/maximum position for best compromised coordination. 2) Replace existing 200A MCB with a 200A MCB with adjustable/static trip to achieve near-coordinated system.
recommendation.quote: BFA recommends set the 200 A MCB Instantaneous trip to High/ maximum position to achieve the Compromised coordination. … BFA recmmends using the 200 A MCB with the Adjustable/ static trip to achieve the almost Coordinated system.
